scope: Explicit lexical variants with shared learning identity. This does not authorize productive prefix stripping or establish equivalence for other senses. Reference entries remain separate in the full dictionary.

variants.evidence: Learn each expression as a whole; do not add お to every noun.
variants.reason: Same everyday object as the already taught base noun; an explicitly taught polite lexical form, not another progress target.

variants.evidence: ご主人 refers respectfully to someone else’s husband.
variants.reason: Explicit recognition and practice of the respectful spouse-reference form after the traditional own-husband usage. Contextual hints distinguish whose husband; not general prefix substitution.

variants.evidence: お見舞い is the common polite form of 見舞い.
variants.reason: Same illness-visit sense as the existing base identity, taught as a whole expression. Does not cover the separate dealing-a-blow sense in the reference entry.

variants.evidence: 非常に means very or extremely.
variants.reason: Explicitly teach the adverb of the base entry’s second, extreme-intensity sense. Earlier emergency-noun instruction does not cover it. Keep the reference adverb distinct without another progress target.

variants.evidence: The written 私 can also be read わたくし in a formal introduction, presentation or other formal exchange.
variants.reason: Same first-person pronoun with an explicitly taught formal reading and contextual hint. This does not cover private affairs, selfishness or other separate senses of the reference entry.
